bullets.title: NVDA: Board probes CEO Jensen Huang over alleged Chinese spy affair; stock -5% premarket
bullets.body: NVDA's board launched an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with a woman US intelligence believes is a Chinese Ministry of State Security asset affiliated with Megaspeed (under export control investigation). The board states no evidence of IP, confidential info, or national security compromise; Huang remains CEO and has committed to full cooperation. Street reaction: Citi maintains Buy/$315 PT (21x C27E), GS maintains Buy with PT raised to $300 at ~11x CY27 EPS of $16.70, Morgan Stanley OW at $300 PT, while Aletheia Capital downgraded to Hold. Polymarket prices Jensen ouster at 17% probability; Republican House members requested a closed-door briefing on Nov 18.

bullets.title: NVDA valuation: Semis SOX -28% in 22 days; GS/MS/UBS see selloff as overdone at trough multiples
bullets.body: The SOX index fell 28% over 22 trading days—one of the largest rolling 1-month drawdowns in history—with NVDA trading at 12-13x CY27 EPS, well below its 10-year median trough of 22x. Goldman raised NVDA PT to $300 and AVGO PT to $540, arguing the selloff prices in ~30-35% EPS cuts that GS/MS view as excessive given intact hyperscaler capex ($1.6-1.75T in 2027). UBS sees semis pricing in ~30% C27 and ~35% C28 EPS cuts. NVDA assembly partners (Hon Hai, Quanta, Wistron) reported Oct revenues +46-118% YoY, signaling intact near-term hardware demand; NVDA results due 11/17.

bullets.title: AMD: Oppenheimer upgrades to Outperform, $600 PT; DC revenue seen +135% in 2027
bullets.body: Oppenheimer's Rick Schafer upgraded AMD to Outperform with a $600 PT (vs. ~15x CY28 EPS, well below the 21x historical average). AMD data center revenue is projected to grow 135% in 2027, representing ~85% of sales, driven by MI455/Helios GPU deployments with visibility into 1H28; GPU revenue expected to overtake EPYC CPUs. OpenAI, Meta, and Anthropic are cited as key demand drivers. AMD is up ~3.5% premarket on the upgrade.

bullets.title: DKNG: Triple-downgraded (JPM, UBS, Stifel) as prediction market losses crater guidance
bullets.body: DraftKings reported a 3Q adjusted EBITDA loss of -$317M vs. Street estimate of -$60M; revenue of $1.33B missed estimates by ~$130M. FY26 EBITDA guidance was cut to $175-275M from $700-900M as prediction market (PM) losses were raised to $650-700M (from $200-300M prior). UBS cut its PT to $22 from $48 and downgraded to Neutral; Citi maintained Buy but cut PT to $22 from $28, citing a 2028 path to $1B+ PM gross profit. NY sports betting data showed DKNG GGR down 1.2% YoY in October with market share contracting 300bps to 31.7% vs. FanDuel gaining 200bps to 44.1%.

bullets.title: GOOGL: New TPU 8tx/8i Max variants launched; JPM removes from focus list, adds META
bullets.body: Google launched four TPU variations—including TPU 8tx for confidential computing and 8i Max for long-context tasks—accelerating its chip release cadence from one every two years to multiple in 2026. JPM notes these are primarily reconfigured SKUs rather than entirely new silicon; AVGO is reportedly designing a 'Blade Runner' TPU anticipated by JPM. Separately, JPM removed GOOGL from its Analyst Focus List (citing Search deceleration to 12% YoY in 3Q from 17% in 2Q) and added META, whose core advertising accelerated +26% YoY in 3Q.

bullets.title: ORCL: Mizuho upgrades to Outperform ($320 PT); $20B financing overhang cleared, 7GW contracted through May 2028
bullets.body: Mizuho upgraded ORCL to Outperform on the AI selloff opportunity, noting the $20B capital raise ($10B debt + $10B equity) removes the major funding overhang. All five mega data center sites are under construction with four permits secured; management has incorporated 1-2 quarter potential delays. ORCL re-contracted older GPUs at ~20% higher pricing even as MSFT wound down its Oracle cloud arrangement. GS also cited ORCL with operational agility and $225B+ FY29-30 revenue targets at 40%+ non-GAAP operating margins.

bullets.title: MNDY: JPM downgrades to Neutral ($87 PT); 4Q guide implies deceleration, NDR softens
bullets.body: Monday.com reported 3Q revenue of $378M (3% beat) with EBIT beating by $30M, but 4Q guidance implies 14% YoY growth vs. 19% in 3Q. Net Dollar Retention moderated to 108% from 109% in 2Q; FCF came in at $16M vs. $66M estimate. JPM cut its rating to Neutral from OW and reduced its PT to $87 from $90, flagging risk of consensus resets for FY27-28 (currently at 15%/14% growth). Citi maintained Buy at $132 PT, arguing cRPO accelerated 5.3pts to +22.3% YoY.

bullets.title: MRVL/LITE deal: Market skeptical on $115B all-stock combination; both stocks hit hard
bullets.body: Wolfe Research questioned the industrial logic of the Marvell-Lumentum deal, with both stocks declining sharply after the announcement. LITE fell -35.9% on the week (worst S&P performer). Jefferies was more constructive, arguing the combination strengthens scale-up and scale-in roadmaps as silicon and optics converge closer to XPUs, with LITE's five NPO designs now targeting 2028-2029 deployments vs. prior 2030+. UBS flagged that the deal raises peak-cycle durability concerns.

bullets.title: APP: Beat; +71% on the week—gaming ad +50% YoY, e-commerce +100%+ YoY
bullets.body: AppLovin was the top S&P performer for the week, surging +71.2%. Morgan Stanley noted APP beat MS estimates by 5% on revenue and 6% on EBITDA, with gaming ad revenue up ~50% YoY and e-commerce surging 100%+ YoY. The stock is now down -41.9% YTD despite the weekly gain.

bullets.title: CHTR: MS maintains EW ($135 PT); Wolfe cuts to $117 on competitive ARPU pressure
bullets.body: Charter reported total residential broadband net losses of -228K, better than estimates of -271K, with mobile adds of +508K vs. +415K expected. Management targets ~$2B opex savings over 18 months plus $1B+ Cox synergies. Morgan Stanley maintained Equal-weight at $135 PT noting Cox integration cutting internet losses in half. Wolfe maintained Underperform, cutting PT to $117 and modeling only ~$1.1B of cost savings realized in 2027, with ARPU facing -2pt headwind if savings are reinvested into pricing.

bullets.title: RBLX: Weekly engagement tracker shows accelerating Y/Y decline; peak CCUs -14% YoY
bullets.body: JPM's engagement tracker showed Roblox platform peak CCUs declined 5% W/W to 23.7M, with Y/Y average peak CCUs now declining 14% through early November, accelerating from -12% in October. Steal An Egg moderated for the 7th consecutive week to 7.7M peak CCUs (down from 14.3M mid-September peak). JPM maintains Neutral at a $53 PT.

bullets.title: CRWV: Letter to Texas Governor-elect on data center construction; key name in AI infra debate
bullets.body: CoreWeave sent a letter to Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa regarding data center construction collaboration, as 22V Research highlighted CRWV can present well by outlining expected revenue per MW of IT capacity and 2027 funding needs. Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa has signaled a suspension of data center approvals pending stronger community protections—a key overhang for the AI infrastructure complex, with MS estimating ~20% of US data center projects (~5GW) will be delayed from 2028 to 2029.

bullets.title: DDOG: Broad-based acceleration; largest customer above minimum commit but F4Q guide conservative
bullets.body: Per JPM Tech Sketch, DDOG's CEO/CFO call showed broad-based core business acceleration with non-AI customer revenue growth; the company adds ~2K gross new logos per quarter. The largest customer consumed materially above its minimum commit in F3Q, but F4Q guidance assumes only the contractual minimum—a potential source of upside that the market may not fully credit.

bullets.title: NET: Best software EPS print; Q4 guide implies 40%+ growth; Wolfe upgrades
bullets.body: Cloudflare posted the best EPS print in Jefferies' software coverage last week, with Q4 guidance implying 40%+ growth. Wolfe Research upgraded NET. The stock also signed a $10M five-year SASE deal with a US Federal cabinet department and a $3M pool win with a multinational. NET appears as a new Trifecta addition at Oppenheimer's technical strategy desk.

bullets.title: TSLA: Cybertruck production shifting toward Cybercab; refunds on deposit backlog
bullets.body: Tesla is shifting Cybertruck production capacity toward the Cybercab given order rates exceeding production capacity ahead of a production shutdown; Tesla is processing refunds on considerable Cybertruck deposits. Additionally, Tesla's China domestic retail collapsed -68% YoY/-86% MoM to ~8.8K units in October while exports surged +66% YoY to 59K units (87% of October wholesale).

bullets.title: FSLR/GNRC: Solar tax credit extensions back on the table; Piper OW both names
bullets.body: Piper Sandler notes the Democratic Congress puts solar tax credit extensions back on the table. Piper reiterates Overweight on FSLR with a $222 PT and GNRC with a $232 PT, flagging NXT as its top pick into the November 16 CMD. The EPC selloff is viewed as overdone with strong 2027 backlog visibility.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro lead times normalize to 1-3 days globally; Duo delayed to late January
bullets.body: JPM's weekly tracker shows iPhone 18 Pro lead times decreased to ~1 day globally (2 days below prior year), indicating broad availability. iPhone 18 Pro Max averaged 9 days globally with US Pro Max still running 6 days above prior year—supporting JPM's price/mix-led revenue thesis. The iPhone Duo remains unavailable for in-store pickup with delivery extending into late January, suggesting constrained supply of the new form factor.

bullets.title: ABNB: +15.6% on the week; 16% room-night growth—largest gap vs. BKNG/EXPE in 5 years
bullets.body: Airbnb was a top S&P performer, gaining +15.6% for the week. Morgan Stanley noted ABNB delivered 16% room-night growth vs. ~12% expected, the largest gap vs. BKNG/EXPE in five years. Jefferies flagged ABNB as a preferred name in internet on encouraging earnings, while Rothschild upgraded to Neutral from Sell.

bullets.title: HF positioning: Tech net-sold 6 straight weeks ($20B+); semis back to Liberation Day lows
bullets.body: Hedge funds sold tech at the fastest pace on record last week, with semis net exposure returning to early-2026/Liberation Day lows (JPM PB data). Levered ETF exposure fell below beginning-of-year levels after $60B+ was sold in a single week. Multi-strat de-grossing was the largest in 20 days since COVID; HF net leverage fell 4% to 12-month lows. QQQ RSI dipped below 30—historically +4% average over the next 5 trading days. JPM strategist Dubravko reiterates YE26 SPX target of 8,000 (8.4% upside from Friday close).

bullets.title: SPHR/LYV: Sphere Orlando likely next; Venue Nation hosting 75M+ fans but AOI under pressure
bullets.body: Per Wolfe/Supino, Sphere management confirmed the next US Sphere project is likely Orlando (possibly at Universal). Live Nation's Venue Nation is expected to host 75M+ fans (+10M vs. 2025), but concerts AOI is declining as fan expectations rise; LYV investor day expected to provide increased disclosure on Venue Nation costs and returns.
